title: How to start selling on Instagram as a UAE business: A guide
summary: In this guide, we’ll explain how to sell on Instagram in 6 steps and how to use payment links to speed up the checkout process for UAE businesses.
body_markdown:
Picture this: A customer discovers your business on Instagram, loves what they see, sends you a DM asking if an item is available, and says they're ready to buy. Then comes the trickier part: figuring out how they'll actually pay you.


For businesses in the UAE, this is a common challenge. While Instagram is a powerful platform for showcasing products, building your brand, and connecting with customers, its native in-app checkout features aren't currently available in the UAE. That means you'll need another way to turn interested followers into paying customers.


In this guide, we'll walk you through how to start selling on Instagram step by step. We'll also show you how payment links can help you accept payments directly from Instagram DMs, Stories, or your bio.


We’ll discuss:


- How to start selling on Instagram: 5 steps


- Apply for a trade license (and possibly an influencer permit)


- Set up an Instagram Professional account and Meta Commerce Manager


- Add your products to Meta Commerce Manager


- Market your shop by tagging products in your posts


- Sell via payment links in DMs and on Instagram Stories


- How to sell on Instagram using Ziina’s Payment Links


Ziina is a payments app built for UAE businesses that need a fast, simple way to accept payments. When you


[sign up with Ziina](https://ziina.app.link/webBlog) , you can share customized payment links over Instagram and receive your funds in just 1-2 business days (and often within 24 hours, subject to bank processing times).


## How to start selling on Instagram in 5 steps


###


### 1. Apply for a trade license (and possibly an influencer permit)


Ready to start selling on Instagram? First, you’ll need to make sure your business has the right licence. Depending on how you plan to sell, you may need one or both of the following:¹


1) Trade license


All businesses in the UAE must have a valid UAE trade license (also called an e-commerce or commercial license). In Dubai, mainland licences are issued by


[Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism](https://www.dubaidet.gov.ae/en/licences-and-permits/business-licensing) (DET). Other emirates have their own licensing authorities.


If you’re setting up your business in one of the UAE’s specialized free zones – such as DMCC or DIFC in Dubai – you can apply for a trade license directly through the relevant free zone authority.


Licensing fees vary depending on the emirate, free zone, permitted activities, visa requirements, and more.


To find out more, read our article:


[The real cost of setting up a business in Dubai](https://ziina.com/blog/cost-of-setting-up-a-business-in-dubai)


2) Influencer license


If you personally publish promotional content for other businesses (like sponsored posts or affiliate promotions), you may need an advertiser permit (also sometimes called an influencer license), which is usually obtained through the


[UAE Media Council](https://uaemc.gov.ae/) .


UAE residents generally need an appropriate trade license before obtaining the permit, though you should check with the relevant authorities for further information.


2


### 2. Set up an Instagram Professional account and Meta Commerce Manager


Your Instagram Professional account is where customers discover your business, while Meta Commerce Manager helps you manage product catalogs and advertising across Meta's platforms.


Start by switching your Instagram profile from a personal account to a professional account. Then complete your profile by adding your logo or profile photo, a business description, contact information, and a link to your website or checkout page.


Next, create or access Meta Commerce Manager through your Meta Business account. From there, you can:


- Create and manage a product catalog


- Connect your catalog to Meta advertising


- Run catalog-based advertising campaigns across Instagram and Facebook


- Sync your catalog from platforms like Shopify


Note:


Meta Shops and some shopping features are only available in supported countries. While businesses in the UAE can use Commerce Manager to manage catalogs and advertising, the full Instagram Shop experience and native checkout aren’t currently available.


### 3. Add your products to Meta Commerce Manager


Your product catalog stores information about your products, including names, descriptions, prices, images, and website links.


If you already sell through Shopify or another supported ecommerce platform, you may be able to sync your catalog automatically.


Meta may also review your catalog and business to ensure they comply with its policies and


[eligibility requirements](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1205792533104321) before certain commerce features become available.


Note:


For UAE businesses, the catalog primarily supports product advertising (rather than a native Instagram Shop checkout experience).


### 4. Market your shop by tagging products in your posts


Now the fun part: marketing your business and actually making your posts shoppable.


Once you have product photos (or promotional material) and go to create a post, tap on “Tag products” before you hit publish. You’ll be able to select products directly from your catalog.


Your customers can access your shop by clicking on a product tag, or by going to your main profile and clicking your website link.


### 5. Sell via payment links in DMs and on Instagram Stories


For UAE-based businesses, Instagram’s native payment processing system isn’t available in the region at the time of writing


July 2026 . Instead of checking out on the app, your customers will be redirected to your online store to finish making their purchase.


This step can come with some friction – for example, a shopper might lose interest while waiting for your website to load or decide not to complete their purchase after being redirected away from Instagram.


An alternative option for your Instagram checkout is to use payment links


, which are shareable URLs that allow your customers to pay you simply by clicking on the link and entering their card details.


On Instagram, you can either send links to customers in one-to-one chats, or you can post them on your Stories to promote a new product to all your followers at once.
